decision: Hold the cached-dimension Q8 reuse candidate, not adopted. An extra scalar-loop stack reload has been removed and ordinary warm allocations reach zero, but whole-generation timing is inconclusive in this session. Restore production to the prior refined Q4 source; retain all candidates, disassembly and samples for remeasurement.

identities.initial_vs_final: Both integrated binaries use the same held runtime bytes. The final test binary adds production Q8 lifetime and inline-callback assertions. Generation measurements use only the final binary.

codegen_findings.method: go tool objdump of saved executables. scripts/summarize_q8_codegen.py identifies the unique backwards BHI loop with four SCVTFWS, four MOVB and four FMADDS instructions, then reports its static extent and stack loads. Parser tests verify the retained disassembly.
codegen_findings.extra_instruction: The rejected range contains MOVD 120(RSP), R10 within the steady four-element scalar loop; the persistent compact closure similarly reloads R11 from120(RSP). The cached variants remove that load. An early description of an extra register-to-register copy was corrected: the salient extra instruction is the stack reload.
codegen_findings.interpretation: Moving shape derivation into the descriptor consumer changes generated register use and introduces a repeated stack load in these Go1.27.3/arm64 builds. A persistent closure without a helper call still has the load and a slowdown, so extra function-call overhead alone is not a sufficient explanation. Precomputing in/out/groups/tiles removes the load even with a range helper. This is a concrete code-generation correlate, not proof that one instruction explains the entire historical5-6% cost. No hardware counters or compiler SSA causal analysis were collected. Equal frame/call-site counts do not imply otherwise identical code or bounds-check placement.

kernel_experiments.shared_arithmetic: All variants preserve the production four-row, paired-remainder and single-row arithmetic, dotQ8PairBlock64 helper, reductions, scale placement, task count, threshold and wide fallback. No column pairing or numerical-tolerance change.

compact.protocol_limitations: Initial diagnostic pass used fixed baseline-then-persistent order and process GOMAXPROCS10, including workers1 leaves. Do not compare absolute times directly with the later pinned pass.

compact_pinned_followup.protocol: Original compact probe binary, -test.cpu=1, workers1 only, three fresh processes, 500ms leaves, fixed within-process mode order. Go omits the CPU suffix in these lines.
compact_pinned_followup.interpretation: Compact slowdown remains with one scheduler thread; the initial GOMAXPROCS setting is not a sufficient explanation. This does not isolate all differences between binaries or remove order bias.

cached_closure.protocol: GOMAXPROCS pinned to executor workers inside leaves; baseline/persistent order reversed in process2. Complete three-process samples retained.
cached_closure.interpretation: Approximately baseline-like scalar-kernel time in this diagnostic batch, not established generation acceleration. Separate probe/callback storage is a cold cost and is excluded from the timed warm kernel.

cached_range.interpretation: Also restores the31-instruction, no-stack-load loop while retaining an extra helper call. Timing became unstable: e.g. workers1/rows1 includes a ratio1.733. Do not use this batch to establish a speedup or exact neutrality.

integrated_candidate.implementation: Shared fp32Kernel descriptor adds in/out/groups/tiles, initialized only for Q8 and unused by FP32/Q4 arithmetic. Ordinary inline Q8 uses a stack descriptor with no callback initialization. Parallel Q8 lazily creates q8Fn, joins, then zeroes the complete shared descriptor. Wide fallback remains before ordinary state/callback setup. Nil-executor dispatch still uses the global parallel path.
integrated_candidate.footprint_scope: 40 extra raw struct bytes:32 for four cached integers and8 for the Q8 callback slot on this architecture. This is not RSS. Workers1 FP32/Q4 generation samples typically add32 allocated bytes because of allocator size classes; the Q8 reduction is much larger but does not erase the fixed-cost tradeoff.
integrated_candidate.correctness: 882 ordinary worker/shape combinations bit-match baselineLinearQ8Into with output guards. Complete state clearing includes all four cached integers. All-workers-blocked completion ordering, same-executor format switching, independent executors, threshold/task-count inline cases and wide fallback without ordinary callback initialization pass. Warm allocation tests cover workers1/2/4 and rows1/2/3/4/5/17.

whole_generation.protocol: After all owned full validation and real-model jobs completed, three fresh before/after blocks with alternating process order;18 fixed format/worker/shape cases, 500ms per leaf, count1, unchanged generation harness. Host activity, memory bandwidth and thermal/power state were not controlled. No other owned heavy job ran during timing; small metadata/parser commands did run.
whole_generation.control_protocol: Three additional alternating label blocks, identical baseline binary on both sides, Q8 prefix33/outputs128 workers1/4,1s leaves. These are independent calibrated estimates, not paired requests.
whole_generation.interpretation: Identical binaries vary substantially, including a1.61 ratio within one control block and large absolute-time shifts. Broad candidate ratios also vary by case/process; neither favorable medians nor unfavorable ones establish a code effect here. Do not claim the historical slowdown is resolved at whole-generation level, a new speedup, or a no-regression guarantee. Allocation reduction is supported independently. The cause of the session's time variation is not established.
